# Code Review Report

## Review Summary

This branch adds two new prose-polish subagents, updates the orchestrator and pipeline docs to dispatch them, and adds two final-edit prompt templates. The overall scope is coherent, but the new agent instructions are not ready to merge: both new subagents document `scene-writer` calls that cannot succeed with the current tool contract, and the final-editor retrieval step cannot actually restrict context to prior chapters as documented.

Files Reviewed: 11
Findings: 2 Critical, 2 Warning, 0 Suggestion

## Findings

### Critical Findings

[C-01] Prose-scrubber revision loop omits the required `sceneNum`
Category: Correctness
Severity: Critical
File: .opencode/agents/prose-scrubber.md
Lines: 44
Description: The new prose-scrubber workflow instructs the agent to call `scene-writer` with only `chapterNum`, `sceneContent`, and `feedback`. That does not match the actual tool contract. In the Python CLI, `revise` dispatches to `cmd_revise(name, chapter_num, scene_num, scene_content, feedback, ...)` and hard-fails when `--scene-num` is missing (`src/tools/scene_writer.py` lines 197-229 and 376-383). As written, the first actionable issue will terminate the scrub pass instead of applying a revision.
Suggestion: Either revise per scene and pass a real `sceneNum`, or switch the design to a chapter-level revision tool that accepts whole-chapter text. If `scene-writer` remains the implementation, update the documented verified contract to include `sceneNum` and restructure the workflow around scene boundaries.

[C-02] Final-editor uses the same invalid `scene-writer` revise contract
Category: Correctness
Severity: Critical
File: .opencode/agents/final-editor.md
Lines: 45, 48
Description: The final-editor workflow repeats the same broken pattern twice, invoking `scene-writer` `operation: "revise"` on whole-chapter text without providing `sceneNum`. The underlying CLI still requires `--scene-num` for every revise call (`src/tools/scene_writer.py` lines 197-229 and 376-383). Any chapter that yields a voice or scrub issue will therefore fail at runtime before the chapter can be written back to story state.
Suggestion: Use a chapter-aware revision mechanism for post-assembly editing, or first map the chapter back to concrete scene numbers and revise scene-by-scene with `sceneNum` populated.

### Warning Findings

[W-01] Final-editor cannot enforce the documented “prior chapters only” RAG query
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: .opencode/agents/final-editor.md
Lines: 41
Description: The workflow says to query “chapters before chapter {N}” and passes `chapterNum: N` to `rag-query`, implying the tool can scope results to earlier chapters. The actual query implementation ignores `chapter_num` entirely during reads and only filters on `content_type` (`src/tools/rag_query.py` lines 116-123). `chapter_num` is stored only as metadata during indexing (`src/tools/rag_query.py` lines 75-76). In practice, the final-editor may retrieve the current chapter or later chapters, which can leak future context into earlier-chapter edits and distort the intended coherence check.
Suggestion: Extend `rag-query` to support metadata filters on `chapter_num` for queries, or remove the misleading `chapterNum: N` guidance and explicitly post-filter results to chapters `< N` before summarizing them.

[W-02] No test covers the new agent-tool contracts
Category: Testing
Severity: Warning
File: tests/unit/test_prompt_relocation.py
Lines: 108-112
Description: The only test change in this branch updates the global prompt file count from the addition of two templates. There is no new test that exercises the prose-scrubber or final-editor workflows against the actual `scene-writer` and `rag-query` contracts, which is why the broken `scene-writer` calls and misleading `chapterNum` usage can pass CI unchanged.
Suggestion: Add focused regression tests for the new subagents' documented tool contracts. At minimum, validate that every documented `scene-writer` revise call includes required arguments and that the final-editor context query excludes chapter `N` and later chapters.

## Overall Assessment

This branch is not ready for merge. The orchestration and documentation updates are directionally correct, but both new runtime instruction files contain executable contract mismatches that will break prose editing as soon as an issue is found. After those are fixed, the branch also needs focused tests around agent-tool integration so future instruction-level regressions are caught before merge.
